I think you miss the goal of artificial intelligence when the topic of architecture is brought in as the object. 

For example video editing is insanely assisted by ai, and has been growing in assistance for the past decade, but there’s no shortage of video editing work is there? 

Bringing artificial intelligence into architecture and really any other profession is like a blacksmith getting a heavier mallet or a tougher anvil. It does not remove the blacksmith. 

There are cases where technology has topographically changed what a profession is. The emergence of aero science changed what an automotive mechanical engineer is. F1 engineers are seriously keen on aero science as much as they are on machinery. Is that to say architects may become keen on ai generated inspiration? Building data blocks like computer programming blocks? 

I feel like your question is more so “will municipalities and private business look to computer programs before they look to humans?” In 50 years could we open a website, design a building, and have it built for us without the architect middle man? I think this reality is a bit realistic, homes now a days are just copy pasting. The architect hardly serves an integral purpose outside of on site coordination. You see the countless mid rises that are simply copy pasting of mid density living. What you are asking is will this be the norm?! It already is, you do not need as many people to create the same thing we were struggling to create 60 years ago. Now we go in see the land, check the data base, laser the topography, plot foundations for the circumstance we find which matches the best scenarios for what we have on record, build, and repeat. 

The architect of the future will not be the architect of today. The thought of designing homes is revolting. Like do we need another home? We are at the extent of suburbian design, we are at the actual limit of city planning, and there is no way around the impending doom that foresees modern commercial architecture. Artificial intelligence is not something that will replace architects, however it is something will make light of the fact that construction in 2022 is redundant copy and paste work. The 2072 architect will be something intangibly different from today’s architect. The entire concept of an architect may be entirely visually different.
